newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN SAYS PLEASED BY CROWN DEVELOPMENTS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN SAYS PLEASED BY CROWN DEVELOPMENTS.

text.p: Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said on Tuesday that he was pleased with the development of the Czech crown and that the current macroeconomic situation was acceptable.

"I think that for the moment (the crown rate) is much better, I am not much afraid of a certain volatility of the Czech crown, of certain limits, but the present situation from a macroeconomic point of view is definitely not bad for us," Pilip told reporters after a meeting of ministers.
Speaking in English, Pilip did not elaborate on what he meant by "certain limits".
He said that the slight improvement in the country's large trade deficit in June was a "signal that after all the external troubles caused to the Czech economy the crown maintains its stability."

The crown came under speculative attack in April and May because of the growing trade problems and the central bank was forced to float the currency, causing it to fall immediately to more than 11 percent below parity with the former mark/dollar basket to which it was pegged.

The crown now shadows the mark. It has fallen more than 30 percent from its 1996 highs agains the dollar, due to the strength of the dollar against the mark. The crown was trading on Tuesday at 34.20 against the dollar.
But the crown has recovered from its lows at more than 19 to the mark to trade late on Tuesday at 18.30 to the dollar.
The depreciation of the crown was credited for a reduction in the trade deficit to 9.6 billion crowns after an 11 billion crown gap in May.
